name: Biology and models of selecting one target among distractors (dragonfly CSTMD1 selective attention, ESTMD facilitation, fly LC10/LC11/LPLC object pathways, LC connectome inputs, LC feature map, figure-ground FD cells)

inputs_state_output: Biology (not a trained ML system, so no 'strong base vs added branch' in the authors' sense): Dragonfly CSTMD1 (B1-B3): input = small-target (ESTMD-like) responses across both eyes, about 1.5 deg dark targets at 40 deg/s; internal state = a local, predictive facilitation 'spotlight' (gain map) centred about 4 deg ahead of the target's last location with surround suppression, building over hundreds of ms and persisting more than 500 ms at the last-seen place, spreading forward during a pause/occlusion (B3 Figs 3-4); output = a single neuron's spike train that follows ONE of two targets (winner-takes-all-like competitive selection with occasional switches; B1 r2=0.83 fit to competitive selection model, B2 bimodal selectivity Fig 2, switching Figs 3-4, models Fig 7). The selected target is chosen by the preceding trajectory (priming, B2 Fig 5) rather than by salience/contrast (B2 Fig 6). There is no appearance-identity channel at all. Fly LC neurons (B5-B7): inputs are columnar medulla/lobula neurons (T2, T2a, T3, Tm, TmY) and lobula intrinsic Li neurons, outputs are glomeruli in the central brain where retinotopy is largely lost (B5); each LC type is a feature detector (LC11 small object, LC4/LPLC2 looming, LC18 objects below lens resolution, LC25 complex line motion; B7). Local FlyWire 783 computation (C09_support/lc_inputs_flywire783.json): fraction of input synapses from the 34 FlyVis output types: LC11 0.458 (T3 0.224, T2 0.146, T2a 0.070), LC17 0.456, LC18 0.500, LC12 0.607, LC4 0.579, LC10a 0.080, LC10d 0.061, LC9 0.017, LPLC2 0.388; fraction from T4/T5: LPLC2 0.311, LPLC1 0.100, all LC types <= 0.002. Remaining inputs come from types not in FlyVis (Li intrinsic neurons e.g. Li15/Li17/Li31/Li33, Tm5f, Tm21, Tm25, TmY31, LT, LC-LC recurrent, central-brain neurons). FD cells (B9): lobula-plate small-field motion cells whose tuning to small objects comes from inhibition by large-field (CH) cells - figure-ground by relative motion. Ours: frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign appearance per detection region vs exemplar/previous target/bank is the strong base; FlyVis gives regional activity of 34 output types (incl. T4/T5) plus 6-neighbour means from a bounded grey crop, with temporal state over exemplar+search frames; two-stage readout identity -> full-box transfer gate. Mapping: insect selection = trajectory-based spatial gain + competition between candidates; our readout = per-candidate identity score + gate. Insects have no analogue of the MASA appearance base; FlyVis has none of the lobula layer (no Li, no LC, no LC10a inputs).
fusion_and_training: Biology: no training; selection is a fixed circuit property. The 'fusion' is multiplicative gain: facilitation raises spike rate by more than 50 % in the focus and lowers it by up to 50 % in the surround, and raises contrast sensitivity more than five-fold (contrast threshold 0.071 -> 0.013, C50 0.36 -> 0.13; B3 Figs 3A, 5C), i.e. the trajectory prior gates the feature response before competition. B2 states a simple winner-takes-all network does not explain the data; a competitive process with switching (best fit: multiple-switch model with 90 % switch probability and 0.75 s time constant, Fig 7) does. Engineering model B4 (ESTMD + facilitation, hand-tuned, untrained): facilitation implemented as a multiplicative gain map around the predicted target position; Bagheri 2015 reports optimal facilitation parameters static in space and dynamic in time, depending on clutter (abstract only). LC11 size/object selectivity relies on inhibitory interactions (background-motion suppression, B5 follow-up), FD cells on inhibition by large-field cells. Nothing here guards a weak branch from being ignored by a learner - there is no learner. Design lesson for ours: the biological cue enters as a GATE/gain on candidate responses keyed to predicted position, not as extra concatenated features; this is equivalent to our tracker prediction + eye centring + gate, not to a new identity branch.
labels_and_loss: None: no training labels or losses in B1-B3, B5-B9 (electrophysiology / calcium imaging / connectomics). B4 is hand-tuned and evaluated against ground-truth target positions only. Hard negatives in biology = a second identical target (B1, B2 use identical 1.5 deg squares differing only by frequency tag/contrast), so the 'similar neighbour' regime is exactly the test condition, but selection is resolved by trajectory history, not by any learned discrimination. No guidance for our identity loss, triplets or class imbalance.
data_camera_resolution_rate: B2: 26 male wild-caught Hemicordulia tau dragonflies; per-figure 4-13 animals, 119-447 trials; LCD monitors 120-165 Hz at 20 cm; 1.5x1.5 deg dark targets on white (337 cd/m2), 40 deg/s vertical, about 20 deg apart, Weber contrast 0.06-1 with frequency tagging (8/12, 11/15 Hz); about 71.4 % of trials pass SNR. B3: n=7-12 dragonflies per experiment, CSTMD1 plus small/large-field STMDs. B5: Drosophila LC11 calcium imaging (dendrite covers about 14-15 columns, about 75 deg; responsive area about 20 deg; responds to a 2.2 deg object). B6: FlyEM hemibrain v1.2.1 (lobula nearly complete, medulla largely missing), 21 LC/LPLC types. B10 (own): FlyWire 783 whole-brain, both hemispheres, e.g. LC11 127 cells / 214,844 input synapses, LC10a 237 / 46,141, LPLC2 210 / 121,557. All stimuli are synthetic, static camera, single or paired tiny targets on uniform or simple background; no natural video, no camera ego-motion, no darkness/glare conditions. B4 used natural panoramic imagery with simulated pursuit (abstract). Far from BDD100K MOT (car-mounted camera, 5 fps labelled frames, large objects, dozens of candidates).
metrics_and_numbers: Authors' metrics, not transferable to our utility/HOTA. B1: competitive selection model fit r2 = 0.83 (abstract, via search record). B2: single-target selectivity index T1 mean 0.68 (sd 0.17), T2 mean -0.58 (sd 0.23); paired-target distribution bimodal with peaks near 0.65 and -0.55 (Fig 2); priming biases selection towards the continuing primed path, P < 0.001 (Fig 5); distracter modulation falls with primer contrast, Kruskal-Wallis chi2 = 21.32, P < 0.001, medium P = 0.006, high P < 0.001, low P = 0.755 (Fig 6); best model multiple switching, 90 % switch probability, 0.75 s time constant (Fig 7). B3: >50 % spike-rate increase in focus (p = 0.0007, n = 9), up to 50 % decrease in surround (p = 0.005) (Fig 3A); peak about 4 deg ahead of target (Fig 4E); no facilitation for a 12 deg jump ahead (Fig 4A); persistence > 500 ms (Fig 4C,E); forward spread after 300 ms pause vs 100 ms p = 0.03, d = 0.7 (Fig 3E); contrast threshold 0.071 -> 0.013, C50 0.36 -> 0.13 (Fig 5C); Cohen d up to about 1.8 (Fig 3D); small-field STMD facilitation > 40 %, large-field about 80 % (Fig 8B,C). B4: outperforms the compared engineering trackers when small moving targets are present and runs at least twice as fast; often locks onto small components of larger objects (abstract only, no numbers checked). B6: T3 major input to LC11/LC17/LC21, T2 to LC4/LC12/LC18; T4/T5 not identified as LC inputs (hemibrain). B10 own numbers: see inputs_state_output (source C09_support/lc_inputs_flywire783.json, keys <type>.fractions.flyvis_output34 and <type>.T4T5_fraction).
distinguishing_ablations: Biological 'ablations' that isolate the selection mechanism: B2 primer vs no-primer (trajectory history alone flips which of two identical targets wins, P < 0.001) and primer-contrast sweep (selection not explained by salience); B3 facilitation tested with jumps/pauses (12 deg jump ahead unfacilitated, matched jump+pause facilitated) - isolates a spatial, predictive gain rather than feature memory. B5 follow-up: LC11 responses suppressed by local background motion (inhibitory interactions isolate the object-vs-background component). No source contains a 'strong appearance base + weak motion branch' ablation; there is no appearance base in insect target selection at all. Negative/limiting results: B2 says simple WTA does not explain the data (needs switching); B2 T1-priming shows later switches to the distracter (lock is not permanent); B4 locks onto parts of larger objects in general scenes (a failure mode directly relevant to large BDD100K objects). Own connectome check (B10) is a structural negative for one hypothesis: LC10a, the Drosophila pathway that pursues ONE moving conspecific among others, gets only 8 % of its input synapses from FlyVis output types and 0.02 % from T4/T5, so it cannot be reconstructed from FlyVis outputs alone; LC11 (46 % from FlyVis outputs, almost all T2/T3/T2a, not T4/T5) partly can.
explanations_addressed: (1) Fly features carry no unique identity information beyond appearance: indirect support (design analogy/caution). In insects, choosing one target among identical distractors relies on trajectory history (B2 Fig 5-6, B3), not on a per-object appearance signature; LC types encode object class/feature (small, looming, line motion; B7) and lose retinotopy at glomeruli (B5), not individual identity. So the biologically expected unique contribution of an optic-lobe model is a trajectory/position prior, which our geometry + Kalman prediction already supply (geometry AUC 0.92-0.93 in project context). (2) Information exists but fusion ignores it (modality imbalance): not addressed; but biology suggests the cue should act as a gain/gate on candidates, which our concatenation into gradient boosting can emulate only if the gating variable (predicted-position offset x fly response) is present. (3) Saved readout features lost it, new activity or fine-tuned core needed: design analogy - facilitation is a per-column spatial map ahead of the target and LC11 integrates about 14-15 columns with centre-surround inhibition; our regional means over a detection box plus 6-neighbour means discard the within-region spatial offset relative to the prediction. A new spatial readout is needed to test it; saved features cannot fully test a column-level facilitation map. (4) FlyVis lacks the lobula object/identity pathway: direct structural evidence from own FlyWire 783 computation - FlyVis has no Li, LC, LPLC, Tm5f/Tm21/Tm25/TmY31 neurons; LC10a (pursuit of one conspecific) is 92 % fed by non-FlyVis types; but LC pathways are object DETECTORS, not identity encoders, so adding them is not expected to fix identity among same-class neighbours. (5) Motion helps only in subsets: design analogy - facilitation in dragonfly helps most at low contrast (contrast threshold 0.071 -> 0.013, B3 Fig 5C) and across short occlusions (forward spread, B3 Fig 3); the corresponding BDD100K regimes are darkness/low contrast and short occlusion with a similar neighbour nearby; test must be stratified, not averaged. (6) Ceiling too low: not addressed by biology; caution that a trajectory gain mostly duplicates the bench's Kalman prior, so its unique share of the +2.8 pp perfect-identity headroom is likely small.
evidence_strength: B1-B3: peer-reviewed (Current Biology, J Neurosci, eLife), one laboratory lineage (O'Carroll/Wiederman), consistent across papers but not independently replicated by another lab; strong for the biological claim 'trajectory-based facilitation + competitive selection'. B4: peer-reviewed engineering, same lab, hand-tuned, small-target regime; weak for MOT. B5-B7: peer-reviewed, strong for LC feature selectivity and inputs; B6 explicitly limited by hemibrain lacking medulla. B9 from memory only. Own FlyWire 783 computation: primary data, reproducible script, but synapse-count fractions include central-brain synapses and do not equal functional drive. Overall for our decision: MODERATE as a negative/design constraint (insects do not solve identity among similar targets by appearance-like lobula features), WEAK as positive evidence that any lobula layer would add identity beyond MASA.
difference_from_tried: Partly different. Tried: frozen MASA cosines + snapped exemplar + PCA products; FlyVis D/C/R1 saved regional features into gradient boosting; neighbour-relative features; tagged previous target; bank; T4/T5 motion consistency; core identity fine-tuning prepared. New relative to that: (a) a per-column predictive facilitation STATE (gain map ahead of the predicted target position, persisting over occlusion, surround suppression) applied INSIDE the fly output before region pooling - the earlier STMD review (A09, research_flyvis_advantage_readout_2026-10-25) already proposed the same facilitation state node, so this item adds the dragonfly selection evidence for it but no new mechanism; (b) a competitive selection between candidates (softmax/WTA with hysteresis over the track's candidates), which is close to what the two-stage readout + ByteTrack assignment already do - no essential difference; (c) a lobula LC-like output layer (LC11/LC12/LC17/LC18-like centre-surround pooling over 14-15 columns of T2/T2a/T3/Tm3/Tm4/TmY3) built from FlyWire 783 weights - new as a FlyVis node, but its inputs are already among our 34 types, so on SAVED regional features it is a linear recombination the gradient boosting could already form; it differs only if computed per column before pooling. LC10a-like pathway cannot be built from FlyVis outputs (8 % input coverage).
math_precheck: All on saved features/query histories, CPU, train26 as the pre-registered check set and fit104 only for fitting. (P1) Regime share and oracle headroom: among candidate sets where appearance-only identity (MASA cosines) picks a wrong region, compute the fraction where the wrong region is a same-class neighbour within the facilitation-relevant zone (e.g. its centre lies closer to the Kalman prediction than the true target or within one box width), and the share of perfect-identity utility (+2.84 pp on train26) carried by those cases (utility of fixing only them). Stop rule: if fixing ALL such cases perfectly is worth < 0.5 pp utility on train26 [threshold is a proposal, to be registered before running], a trajectory-gain node cannot matter for the +2 pp criterion. (P2) Complementarity vs no-fly prior: for appearance-error cases, compare rank-1 accuracy of (a) geometry/Kalman distance alone, (b) R1 eye-input features, (c) FlyVis D features, (d) an LC-proxy = fixed FlyWire-783-weighted sum of saved T2/T2a/T3/Tm3/Tm4/TmY3 regional activity minus 6-neighbour mean; paired bootstrap over videos. Stop if (c) and (d) are not better than (a) and (b) with CI excluding 0 on train26. (P3) Conditional information: cross-fitted log-loss gain (or CMI estimate) of adding FlyVis/LC-proxy to appearance + geometry + R1, restricted to the P1 ambiguous subset and stratified by low-light/glare/occlusion tags; stop if the gain over R1 has CI including 0 in every stratum. (P4) Facilitation feasibility without new maps: from saved per-frame target positions only, compute a pure trajectory facilitation score (Gaussian gain centred ahead of the predicted position with surround suppression, persistence over missed frames) - this is the no-fly version; if adding it to appearance + geometry gives no utility gain, the fly version (same gain applied to fly activity) needs a separate justification that the fly response itself, not the position prior, discriminates. Only if P1 headroom >= threshold AND P2/P3 show fly > R1 in the ambiguous regime, proceed to generate new per-column FlyVis maps on GPU. Expectation stated honestly: biology predicts the unique part is the position prior, so P4 (no fly) is likely to capture whatever P2-P3 find.
cue_role_and_regime: Role in biology: a GATE/gain (multiplicative spatial spotlight on candidate responses keyed to predicted trajectory, with surround suppression) feeding a competitive per-target selector with memory (persistence > 500 ms, forward spread over occlusion); LC-like layers act as feature detectors per candidate (small object, looming), not identity. Targeted regime: two or more similar small targets close in space (about 20 deg apart in B2), low contrast (facilitation lowers contrast threshold five-fold), brief occlusion/pause, clutter (LC11 background-motion suppression, FD figure-ground by relative motion). Mapped to BDD100K MOT: same-class neighbours with similar look near the prediction, darkness/low contrast, short occlusion, cluttered background with ego-motion. Crossing paths with swapped trajectories is NOT handled well by this mechanism: it boosts whatever is at the predicted place (B2 shows switches to distracter, B4 locks onto parts of larger objects).
no_fly_equivalent_control: Cheapest equivalents with the same role and capacity: (1) pure trajectory spotlight score from the Kalman prediction (Gaussian gain ahead of predicted centre, surround suppression, decaying persistence over missed frames) - parameter count comparable to a facilitation state (a few scalars); (2) velocity-direction consistency (OC-SORT-style) and IoU/distance to prediction already in geometry; (3) eye-input R1 regional features passed through the identical LC-proxy weights (same linear form, no FlyVis dynamics) for the LC-layer variant; (4) an equal-size random projection / small MLP on R1 for the competitive-selection variant. Three-way comparison required: appearance+geometry (base) / base + no-fly spotlight or R1-LC-proxy / base + fly spotlight or fly LC-proxy.
bio_node_mapping: Mechanisms map to nodes outside the current FlyVis model: STMD facilitation (dragonfly lobula CSTMD1 and upstream small/large-field STMDs) -> FlyVis STATE node (a recurrent gain map over output columns); lobula LC11/LC12/LC17/LC18/LC4 -> new READOUT/output layer on T2/T2a/T3/Tm3/Tm4/TmY3 (all among the 34 FlyVis outputs); LPLC2 -> T4/T5-fed looming layer (31 % of input synapses from T4/T5 in FlyWire 783); LC10a (single-target pursuit) -> mostly non-FlyVis inputs (92 %), not buildable; FD cells -> lobula-plate figure-ground (blowfly, no direct Drosophila connectome type mapped here). Connectome data: yes, FlyWire 783 present locally (E:/Dissertation/data/flywire/783), counts computed in C09_support/lc_inputs_flywire783.json; Li inhibitory interneurons that shape LC selectivity are in FlyWire but absent from FlyVis.
novelty_overlap: Nearest prior: STMD/facilitation trackers (Bagheri et al. 2015-2017; Wang/Yue STMD feedback, reviewed in A09) and connectome-constrained LC models (Cowley et al. 2024 [uncertain]); our version would differ by putting an LC-like layer/facilitation state on the connectome-constrained FlyVis outputs and testing it as identity among same-class neighbours in MOT with a no-fly control - does not stop the work.
candidate_node_change: Two candidate nodes, ranked. (A, preferred, cheapest) READOUT: lobula LC-like layer on top of FlyVis outputs. For each candidate region compute, per FlyVis column inside and around the region, LC-type responses with FlyWire 783 input weights (LC11: T3/T2/T2a; LC12: Tm3/Tm4/T2/TmY3; LC17/LC18: T2a/T3/T2; LC4: T2/TmY3/Tm4; LPLC2: T4/T5 + Tm5f-free subset), dendritic pooling over about 14-15 columns, and a centre-surround inhibition standing in for missing Li neurons (one learned scalar per LC type); pool to the region and feed the existing identity stage. Fixes FlyVis problem: FlyVis stops at the medulla/lobula output columns and has no object-level layer, so object/background segregation is left to an external head. Equal controls: appearance only; appearance + stock C; appearance + R1 through the same LC weights; appearance + equal-capacity random-weight LC layer (shuffled connectome weights, same column pooling). Caveat: on saved regional features (A) is a linear recombination of existing inputs, so a CPU test on saved features can only show a null; a real test needs per-column activity (new maps). (B) STATE: predictive facilitation gain map over output columns (same as A09 proposal) - justified by B2/B3 as the insect mechanism for selecting one of identical targets. Condition to proceed to GPU (new per-column maps on train26 + val, one 12 GB GPU, single CUDA process): math_precheck P1 headroom >= registered threshold AND P2/P3 show fly LC-proxy > R1 LC-proxy with CI excluding 0 in the ambiguous subset of train26; otherwise record 'biology predicts position prior, already in the bench' and do not run.
strongest_objection: Insect biology does not show an identity mechanism among similar targets that uses appearance-like features: dragonfly CSTMD1 selects one of two identical targets by trajectory history and a predictive spatial gain, and LC neurons are class/feature detectors whose glomerular outputs lose retinotopy. Both functions are already in our bench in engineered form (Kalman prediction, eye centring on the prediction, ByteTrack assignment, geometry features with AUC 0.92-0.93), so the most biologically faithful additions are likely to duplicate the no-fly position prior and fail the (fly + X) > (X without fly) rule; the facilitation also boosts whichever object occupies the predicted location, which is precisely the wrong-neighbour failure. In addition, the most relevant Drosophila pursuit pathway (LC10a) is 92 % fed by neurons FlyVis does not model, so a faithful lobula extension would need a large model expansion beyond 734 parameters with no evidence it helps identity.
cost_and_hardware: CPU on saved features: P1-P4 a few hours (no training of the core). Connectome-weight extraction already done (minutes, local FlyWire 783). New per-column FlyVis activity maps for an LC-like readout or facilitation state: one 12 GB GPU, comparable to earlier map-generation runs over train26 + val (hours), single CUDA process. Faithful lobula extension with Li interneurons and retraining FlyVis: days and a new model - not justified by this evidence.
